currentContext.strengths: Integrated campus model at a major Mumbai transit hub (metro, rail, road access) combining real estate, exhibitions, events and hospitality into one ecosystem|100% occupancy on LEED Platinum-certified, renewable-energy-powered Grade-A office towers with long-term leases to multinational tenants and a tenant NPS of 94.80; more than six clients renewed for a further five-year term in the year|Scale leadership in exhibitions — 70,000+ sq. mt. venue with newly operational Hall 6 (18,000+ capacity), described as hosting more exhibitions/events at greater scale than any private venue of its kind in India|Indabrator's 60+ year engineering heritage and 2,500+ installations across railways, defence, steel and heavy engineering, having introduced shot-blasting technology to India in 1964|Debt-free balance sheet with strong internal cash generation, funding new capex (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, Wayside Amenities) through internal accruals|Early-mover positioning in the newly awarded Wayside Amenities vertical (9 sites in possession, 3 corridors) ahead of the broader national roll-out targeted by highway authorities
currentContext.strategies: Cost optimisation across the campus — reducing energy use (lighting, HVAC, real-time monitoring), consolidating procurement across businesses under a common Supplier Code of Conduct, and reviewing costs at set intervals against performance.|Efficiency for scalable growth — deploying systems that give clearer operational visibility at Nesco Center, building workforce capability for new verticals (Wayside Amenities, My Water Box, Décor line), and reworking Indabrator's manufacturing processes to cut waste and shorten production cycles.|Operational reliability — preventive maintenance schedules across facilities and equipment, consistent quality checks across infrastructure delivery, event execution and manufacturing, and structured tracking/resolution of operational risk across supply chain, regulatory compliance and construction.|Driving revenue growth by building new business capabilities out of existing strengths (Wayside Amenities from food/service capability, My Water Box from events/hospitality demand), expanding food and hospitality nationally beyond Mumbai, and strengthening the Nesco campus as an integrated destination.|ESG and responsible growth is named as the fifth strategic pillar (detail captured under the risks_esg domain).|Indabrator: grow the order book while running leaner — build out the marketing/sales team to widen the pipeline, hold firm on cost control across manufacturing and procurement to protect margins, streamline operations via system implementation, and stay selective on orders favouring clear execution and healthy margins.|Nesco Foods: keep widening footprint across restaurants, catering, beverages and décor — scale what already works, serve events more efficiently, and open new revenue streams wherever demand is clear.|Wayside Amenities: build out sites across expressway corridors to the Nesco service standard as the company's first move beyond the Mumbai campus at scale, positioning it as a fresh revenue stream over the next few years.|CFO priority: as the business enters a more capital-intensive cycle, focus remains on prudent capital allocation, efficient deployment of resources and investments that support sustainable long-term growth, while preserving the debt-free balance sheet.|Company follows a practice of returning substantial free cash flow to shareholders via dividends, governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy aligned with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. A final dividend of Rs 7.00 per equity share (face value Rs 2) was recommended for FY26, up from Rs 6.50 per share in FY25, subject to AGM approval. The Company remained debt-free through FY26 and maintains adequate cash reserves under a disciplined working-capital management framework; new capex (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, Wayside Amenities) is planned to be funded entirely through internal accruals/reserves rather than debt, and the CFO has flagged prudent capital allocation and efficient resource deployment as the priority as the business enters a more capital-intensive cycle.
currentContext.expansion: Nesco Realty: with Towers 3 and 4 at full occupancy, the company has begun expanding the Nesco Center campus with Tower 2 — 5.01 mn sq. ft. total constructed area, of which 2.50 mn sq. ft. is chargeable premium office space, plus an integrated hotel (700+ premium rooms and suites, 150+ serviced apartments) designed to rank among India's largest hotel developments by room count, along with restaurants, cafes, banquet halls and wellness/fitness centres. The Intimation of Disapproval (IOD) has been received from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, clearing the project to move forward; construction is to commence immediately on receiving final clearances, with a duration of about 60 months from commencement, funded through reserves and accruals. Bombay Exhibition Center: Hall 6 (13,400+ sq. mtr. of exhibition space, 18,000+ visitor capacity, with basement parking) became the venue's latest expansion and is now fully operational, taking BEC to six operational halls. A redevelopment plan covers roughly 60% of BEC's current capacity, to be executed in two phases with Phase 1 expected to begin shortly, aimed at upgrading infrastructure, enhancing customer experience and widening the venue to concerts, sports and other large-format events alongside exhibitions. Wayside Amenities: construction has begun on four sites of the Hyderabad-Visakhapatnam Expressway (Khammam-Devarapalli Section), part of 9 sites across express corridors awarded via 3 NHLML tenders. Separately, the BRSR discloses that 4.34% of the Company's capital expenditure in FY26 (17.03% in FY25) went toward specific technologies improving environmental and social impact, described as investment in equipment for improved maintenance, safety, working conditions and security.
currentContext.mdna: Wayside Amenities rides two structural trends: a fast-expanding national expressway network and the need for better roadside infrastructure to match it, plus rising highway connectivity and vehicle traffic driving demand for organised traveller services.|Nesco Foods demand is driven by busier campus activity feeding steady demand for food and event services, and by growth through outdoor catering, restaurant partnerships and event-linked demand beyond the campus.|Indabrator's order pipeline is being widened through a larger marketing/sales team, targeting customers in railways, defence and heavy engineering who value price-competitive, quality-consistent, faster-delivery domestic supply.|Management explicitly flags the business entering a 'more capital-intensive cycle' (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, Wayside Amenities), with financial discipline aimed at preserving the debt-free balance sheet through prudent capital allocation.|Indabrator is focused on growing its order book by building out its marketing team to widen the pipeline and bring in new orders, while staying selective on the orders it takes — favouring those with clear execution and healthy margins.|Wayside Amenities: 3 tenders awarded by National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML) across 9 sites on express corridors; 4 sites are in active development, with construction begun on four sites of the Hyderabad–Visakhapatnam Expressway (Khammam–Devarapalli Section). The business remains pre-revenue (development stage), with first revenue expected in the later part of FY 2026-27 as sites become operational.

risks.note: The Company operates across six structurally distinct verticals — commercial real estate, exhibitions, events, hospitality and food services, engineering and wayside amenities — each with its own risk profile, cyclicality and external sensitivities. Governing this mix requires the Company to run a formal Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework embedded across every business unit, aggregating heterogeneous exposures (strategic, operational, compliance and financial, each rated high/medium/low by probability and impact) that would otherwise be managed as separate businesses.

one-line thesis: Nesco has accelerated its transformation from a Mumbai-centric real estate player into a multi-vertical experience economy operator, with major new revenue streams from highway wayside amenities and Tower 2’s integrated hotel-office complex now on the cusp of execution, fundamentally reshaping its growth profile and valuation drivers.
financial scorecard: revenue: +8% YoY (Rs.845cr); EBITDA/margin: +3.4% YoY, margin stable at ~65%; PAT (rptd): +3.8% YoY (Rs.375cr); PAT (normalized): same (no one-offs); order book: Rs.3,500cr capex pipeline (Tower 2 + 11 WSA sites); net debt: Rs.0 (debt-free, Rs.1,100cr liquidity)
guidance: revenue growth: >20% CAGR over 3-5 years (driven by Tower 2, WSA, BEC); margin: target 65%+ EBITDA margin across new verticals; order inflow: 11 WSA sites secured (Rs.100cr/site revenue potential); capex/commissioning: Rs.3,500cr over next 5 years, Tower 2 construction to commence late FY26, WSA sites to commission Q4FY27-Q1FY28
order book & pipeline: Rs.3,500cr total capex commitment: Rs.3,500cr for Tower 2 (IT + hotel) + Rs.1,100cr implied capex for 11 WSA sites (Rs.100cr/site avg) = Rs.4,600cr total project pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: Nesco Realty: Tower 3 & 4 at 100% occupancy; Tower 2 (IOD secured) to add 1.6M sq.ft IT + 750-room hotel; BEC: Rs.175cr revenue, 50%+ EBITDA margin, Hall 6 operational; Nesco Foods: 16% growth, 50+ brand partnerships; Indabrator: Rs.50cr revenue, 3 WSA tenders secured; WSA: 11 sites awarded (4 Hyderabad-Vizag, 3 Bangalore-Chennai, 4 Raipur-Vizag), 8-10% blended margin
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 50+ additional highway corridors; REIT listing of Tower 2 or BEC assets; franchising Nesco Foods model; scaling Indabrator’s WSA tech platform to third-party operators
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin stable at ~65% despite new verticals; WSA margins expected at 8-10% (fuel 3-3.5%, F&B 20%); Tower 2 hotel projected at 55-60% EBITDA margin (conservative ARR Rs.15,000/night); no material input cost inflation cited
capex / expansion: Rs.3,500cr allocated to Tower 2 (IT + hotel) over next 5 years; Rs.1,100cr implied for 11 WSA sites (Rs.100cr/site); maintenance capex not disclosed but implied within total Rs.780cr FY25 capex (mostly Tower 2)
capital allocation: 10% dividend payout (Rs.6.50/share); remaining cash (Rs.1,100cr liquidity) to fund Tower 2 and WSA capex; no share buybacks or M&A mentioned; no REIT plan confirmed but acknowledged as a future possibility
risks & watch-items: Delays in Tower 2 commencement due to litigation over approvals; WSA site execution delays due to land acquisition or state-level bureaucracy; competition in premium office space from new Mumbai supply; margin compression in BEC if demand softens
management quality / tone: Confident, visionary, and disciplined; emphasizes long-term value creation over leverage; acknowledges debt potential but prioritizes safety; proactive on ESG and digital adoption; responsive to shareholder feedback on virtual AGMs
non-obvious takeaways: Wayside amenities (WSA) are not just fuel stops but integrated experience hubs with F&B, retail, and hospitality — a defensible moat in rural-urban corridor development; Nesco’s 100% green power (not solar) is sourced via PPAs, making it a rare ESG leader in real estate without rooftop panels

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A Mumbai-based diversified conglomerate anchored by an integrated real estate, exhibitions, events and hospitality campus (Nesco Center), alongside a surface-preparation engineering business (Indabrator) and a newly launched wayside-amenities vertical along national expressways.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Nesco operates six businesses from its flagship integrated campus, Nesco Center in Goregaon (East), Mumbai: commercial real estate leasing (Nesco Realty - IT Park Towers 3 & 4), exhibition and event venue hosting (Bombay Exhibition Center), owned live-event formats (Nesco Events), hospitality and F&B across the campus and off-site (Nesco Foods), and, from FY26, roadside food/retail/fuel amenities along national expressway corridors (Wayside Amenities). Separately, its Indabrator division manufactures shot-blasting machines, paint booths, abrasives and spares from two facilities in Gujarat, serving foundry, railway, automotive, defence, shipbuilding and chemical customers in India and select export markets.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Nesco Retail Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary incorporated 21 February 2025 to pursue opportunities in hospitality, realty and related amenity businesses across India; continues to evaluate projects and opportunities aligned with its strategic objectives.
- Nesco Foundation for Innovation and Development (NFID) — subsidiary: Under voluntary liquidation pursuant to Section 59 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, w.e.f. 20 October 2023; other formalities of liquidation are underway.
- Patel Consultancy Services Pvt Ltd — related party: Entity in which Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence.

segment_detail.body: Nesco Realty: Tower 3 & 4 at 100% occupancy; Tower 2 (IOD secured) to add 1.6M sq.ft IT + 750-room hotel; BEC: Rs.175cr revenue, 50%+ EBITDA margin, Hall 6 operational; Nesco Foods: 16% growth, 50+ brand partnerships; Indabrator: Rs.50cr revenue, 3 WSA tenders secured; WSA: 11 sites awarded (4 Hyderabad-Vizag, 3 Bangalore-Chennai, 4 Raipur-Vizag), 8-10% blended margin

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Nesco Realty:** Grade-A leased office space, IT Park Towers 3 & 4
- **Bombay Exhibition Center:** Exhibition halls (incl. Hall 6, 18,000+ capacity), MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, Exhibitions) venue hosting
- **Nesco Events:** Corporate events, Concerts (incl. multi-city, off-campus), Navratri (proprietary IP/format)
- **Nesco Foods:** Food courts, cafeterias and restaurants, Banquets and mass catering (Gourmet Craft), Event decor, My Water Box (alkaline packaged water)
- **Indabrator:** Shot-blasting machines, Paint booths, Abrasives, Spare parts for shot-blasting machines
- **Wayside Amenities:** Roadside retail, Food and convenience services, Fuel services for expressway travellers

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Mumbai / India (primary delivery location for Realty, Foods and BEC businesses)
- 23 States and 7 Union Territories (domestic sales footprint, FY26)
- Exports (Indabrator only): UAE, Austria, China, Germany, France, Sri Lanka, Netherlands, Oman, Uganda — 0.07% of total turnover

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: >20% CAGR over 3-5 years (driven by Tower 2, WSA, BEC); margin: target 65%+ EBITDA margin across new verticals; order inflow: 11 WSA sites secured (Rs.100cr/site revenue potential); capex/commissioning: Rs.3,500cr over next 5 years, Tower 2 construction to commence late FY26, WSA sites to commission Q4FY27-Q1FY28

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into 50+ additional highway corridors; REIT listing of Tower 2 or BEC assets; franchising Nesco Foods model; scaling Indabrator’s WSA tech platform to third-party operators

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Wayside Amenities rides two structural trends: a fast-expanding national expressway network and the need for better roadside infrastructure to match it, plus rising highway connectivity and vehicle traffic driving demand for organised traveller services.
- Nesco Foods demand is driven by busier campus activity feeding steady demand for food and event services, and by growth through outdoor catering, restaurant partnerships and event-linked demand beyond the campus.
- Indabrator's order pipeline is being widened through a larger marketing/sales team, targeting customers in railways, defence and heavy engineering who value price-competitive, quality-consistent, faster-delivery domestic supply.
- Management explicitly flags the business entering a 'more capital-intensive cycle' (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, Wayside Amenities), with financial discipline aimed at preserving the debt-free balance sheet through prudent capital allocation.
- Indabrator is focused on growing its order book by building out its marketing team to widen the pipeline and bring in new orders, while staying selective on the orders it takes — favouring those with clear execution and healthy margins.
- Wayside Amenities: 3 tenders awarded by National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML) across 9 sites on express corridors; 4 sites are in active development, with construction begun on four sites of the Hyderabad–Visakhapatnam Expressway (Khammam–Devarapalli Section). The business remains pre-revenue (development stage), with first revenue expected in the later part of FY 2026-27 as sites become operational.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin stable at ~65% despite new verticals; WSA margins expected at 8-10% (fuel 3-3.5%, F&B 20%); Tower 2 hotel projected at 55-60% EBITDA margin (conservative ARR Rs.15,000/night); no material input cost inflation cited

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: 10% dividend payout (Rs.6.50/share); remaining cash (Rs.1,100cr liquidity) to fund Tower 2 and WSA capex; no share buybacks or M&A mentioned; no REIT plan confirmed but acknowledged as a future possibility

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Nesco Realty: with Towers 3 and 4 at full occupancy, the company has begun expanding the Nesco Center campus with Tower 2 — 5.01 mn sq. ft. total constructed area, of which 2.50 mn sq. ft. is chargeable premium office space, plus an integrated hotel (700+ premium rooms and suites, 150+ serviced apartments) designed to rank among India's largest hotel developments by room count, along with restaurants, cafes, banquet halls and wellness/fitness centres. The Intimation of Disapproval (IOD) has been received from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, clearing the project to move forward; construction is to commence immediately on receiving final clearances, with a duration of about 60 months from commencement, funded through reserves and accruals. Bombay Exhibition Center: Hall 6 (13,400+ sq. mtr. of exhibition space, 18,000+ visitor capacity, with basement parking) became the venue's latest expansion and is now fully operational, taking BEC to six operational halls. A redevelopment plan covers roughly 60% of BEC's current capacity, to be executed in two phases with Phase 1 expected to begin shortly, aimed at upgrading infrastructure, enhancing customer experience and widening the venue to concerts, sports and other large-format events alongside exhibitions. Wayside Amenities: construction has begun on four sites of the Hyderabad-Visakhapatnam Expressway (Khammam-Devarapalli Section), part of 9 sites across express corridors awarded via 3 NHLML tenders. Separately, the BRSR discloses that 4.34% of the Company's capital expenditure in FY26 (17.03% in FY25) went toward specific technologies improving environmental and social impact, described as investment in equipment for improved maintenance, safety, working conditions and security.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, visionary, and disciplined; emphasizes long-term value creation over leverage; acknowledges debt potential but prioritizes safety; proactive on ESG and digital adoption; responsive to shareholder feedback on virtual AGMs

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated campus model at a major Mumbai transit hub (metro, rail, road access) combining real estate, exhibitions, events and hospitality into one ecosystem
- 100% occupancy on LEED Platinum-certified, renewable-energy-powered Grade-A office towers with long-term leases to multinational tenants and a tenant NPS of 94.80; more than six clients renewed for a further five-year term in the year
- Scale leadership in exhibitions — 70,000+ sq. mt. venue with newly operational Hall 6 (18,000+ capacity), described as hosting more exhibitions/events at greater scale than any private venue of its kind in India
- Indabrator's 60+ year engineering heritage and 2,500+ installations across railways, defence, steel and heavy engineering, having introduced shot-blasting technology to India in 1964
- Debt-free balance sheet with strong internal cash generation, funding new capex (Tower 2, hall redevelopment, Wayside Amenities) through internal accruals
- Early-mover positioning in the newly awarded Wayside Amenities vertical (9 sites in possession, 3 corridors) ahead of the broader national roll-out targeted by highway authorities

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delays in Tower 2 commencement due to litigation over approvals; WSA site execution delays due to land acquisition or state-level bureaucracy; competition in premium office space from new Mumbai supply; margin compression in BEC if demand softens

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Wayside amenities (WSA) are not just fuel stops but integrated experience hubs with F&B, retail, and hospitality — a defensible moat in rural-urban corridor development; Nesco’s 100% green power (not solar) is sourced via PPAs, making it a rare ESG leader in real estate without rooftop panels

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Cost optimisation across the campus — reducing energy use (lighting, HVAC, real-time monitoring), consolidating procurement across businesses under a common Supplier Code of Conduct, and reviewing costs at set intervals against performance.
- Efficiency for scalable growth — deploying systems that give clearer operational visibility at Nesco Center, building workforce capability for new verticals (Wayside Amenities, My Water Box, Décor line), and reworking Indabrator's manufacturing processes to cut waste and shorten production cycles.
- Operational reliability — preventive maintenance schedules …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TCS and IT firms may reduce office space demand | DLF | loser | Low | Nesco’s premium, experience-driven spaces and captive demand from events/F&B reduce reliance on IT tenants |
| Nesco’s WSA model disrupts traditional highway rest stops | IRCTC | beneficiary | Medium | Nesco’s WSA could become preferred partner for highway hospitality, potentially replacing IRCTC’s existing model |
